facile

FASS-ul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Facile is effortlessly done without any real depth.

The politician's facile solution to the housing crisis ignored every complicated factor driving it.

Example

The reviewer dismissed the essay's conclusion as facile, since it ignored every counterargument entirely.

Facile describes something -- an answer, a solution, an argument -- that seems easy or quick on the surface but fails to address the real complexity underneath.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

simplistic: Simplistic means oversimplified -- a treatment that flattens a complicated subject into something too neat to be true. Facile adds a note of slick effortlessness: a facile answer not only shortchanges the complexity, it glides by looking smooth, quick, and easy.

shallow: Shallow means staying on the surface, and it can describe people, feelings, or ideas. Facile is a narrower, more bookish criticism aimed at answers and arguments: it says a response came easily precisely because it dodged every real difficulty.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

thorough: complete and detailed

exacting: strict and demanding in method

Where it sits · how shallow the ease really is

quick → facile → glib

quick vs. facile: A quick answer is simply fast, and speed by itself is no flaw; facile goes further, charging that the answer is easy only because it skips every hard part.

glib vs. facile: Glib goes a step further than facile: a facile answer is too easy and thin, while a glib one is delivered with so much smooth, salesman-like polish that the emptiness feels almost insulting.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — fac: to do or make (Latin (facere))

suffix — -ile: capable of, tending to (Latin)

Put it together: fac ("to do or make") + -ile ("capable of") = easily done -- and, by extension, done too easily to be taken seriously.

Use the root in a new word: factory: The same root gives us "factory," a place where things are made -- both words trace back to the Latin verb for "to make."

Strength Check

Word Choice

Facile is a critical, somewhat literary word -- it almost always signals disapproval of an answer that dodges real complexity, so it fits sharp critiques better than casual chat.
